result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers turn the switch into an accessible `<button role="switch">` with `aria-checked` and keep the `/api/prefs` payload. A has a real bug: a top-level `var status` in a classic script hits the legacy `window.status` string property, so its "Saved." and error messages never appear. B's `const` avoids that, so its Saving/Saved/error feedback works, and B also styles the Save button more fully, though it keeps the faint #ccc off state and doesn't add a custom focus ring to Save. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers turn the switch into a proper `<button role="switch">` with `aria-checked`, a label and keyboard support, and both keep the original /api/prefs payload. B's save feedback is broken: `var status` at the top level of a classic script binds to the legacy `window.status` property and turns the element into a string, so the 'Saved.' and error messages never appear. A's `const status` avoids that bug. A also styles the Save button, though it keeps the faint #ccc off track, while B darkens the track and adds an explicit focus ring on Save.
